clinician.final_diagnosis: acute PK secondary to an acute spontaneous idiopathic left renal subcapsular hematoma that became infected
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old female presented with symptoms including lethargy, vomiting, lower back pain, flank pain, dysuria, urinary frequency, malodorous urine, hyperglycemia, fever, and left costovertebral angle tenderness. Urinalysis revealed findings consistent with a urinary tract infection (small leukocyte esterase, 21-50 WBCs/HPF). A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis without contrast identified a large subcapsular hematoma of the left kidney. Urine culture grew Candida glabrata. An initial chest X-ray showed left lower lobe consolidation with pleural effusion. Subsequently, an ultrasound-guided aspiration of the left subcapsular fluid collection was performed. Cultures from this aspirated fluid grew Klebsiella pneumonia, confirming the infection of the renal subcapsular hematoma. Despite aspiration, there was no clinical improvement, and the size of the subcapsular renal abscess remained unchanged on subsequent CT.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with symptoms suggestive of pyelonephritis and UTI, including fever, flank pain, CVA tenderness, dysuria, and urinary frequency.
Urinalysis showed evidence of urinary tract infection with leukocyte esterase and white blood cells.
CT scan without contrast identified a large subcapsular hematoma of the left kidney.
An ultrasound-guided aspiration of the left subcapsular fluid collection was performed, which was described as a subcapsular renal abscess.
Cultures from the aspirated subcapsular fluid grew Klebsiella pneumonia, confirming the infection of the hematoma.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Culture of aspirated fluid from the hematoma grew Klebsiella pneumonia (E013).
Presence of systemic symptoms, flank pain, CVA tenderness, and a large infected renal subcapsular hematoma (E006, E013).

remaining_uncertainties: Complete blood count (CBC) and comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP) results were not documented, which would provide information on systemic inflammation and renal function.
Results from a CT scan with contrast were not documented, which could have provided more definitive imaging evidence of acute pyelonephritis or abscess characteristics.
The 'spontaneous idiopathic' nature of the hematoma's origin is stated in the diagnosis but not explicitly supported by documented evidence.
The precise temporal relationship and pathogenic link between the Candida glabrata UTI and the Klebsiella pneumonia infection of the hematoma are not fully detailed.
